title: With Earnest Longings of the Mind
description: With Earnest Longings of the Mind in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 42, part 1, headed “Desertion and hope; or, Complaint of absence from public worship”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: With ear-nest long-ings of the mind, My God, to thee I look; So pants the hunt-ed hart to find And taste the cool-ing brook.

lines: With earnest longings of the mind,
My God, to thee I look;
So pants the hunted hart to find
When shall I see thy courts of grace,
So long an absence from thy face
Then to thy house did numbers go,
And all our work was praise.
But why, my soul, sunk down so far
Why do my thoughts indulge despair,
Hope in the Lord, whose mighty hand
For I shall yet before him stand,

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
